title: Error Boundaries: Catching UI Crashes
description: Learn how React error boundaries prevent the whole app from crashing and how Next.js makes them easy.

slides.title: The White Screen of Death 💀
slides.content:
# When React Components Throw

If a component throws an error during rendering, React unmounts the entire tree. Users see a blank white page.

In vanilla React, you wrap components in an **error boundary** class component that catches errors and shows a fallback UI.

Next.js takes this further with built‑in `error.js` files and the `reset()` function for recovery.

slides.title: Classic React Error Boundary (components/ErrorBoundary.js)

quizData.question: What errors do React error boundaries catch?

options.text: All errors in the app, including event handlers and async code
Errors during rendering, in lifecycle methods, and in constructors of child components

quizData.explanation: Error boundaries catch errors in the render phase. They don't catch errors in event handlers, async code, or on the server.

slides.title: Next.js App Router: `error.js` 📄
Segment Error Page (app/dashboard/error.js)
slides.content: Shows a friendly message and a retry button.

quizData.question: What does the `reset` function in an error boundary do?

options.text: Re‑renders the error boundary's children, attempting recovery

quizData.explanation: `reset()` re‑mounts the error boundary’s content, giving the component a second chance (e.g., after a network hiccup).

slides.title: Granular vs Global Boundaries 🪆
slides.content:
# Nesting Errors

* Place `error.js` at the segment level to catch errors only in that segment.
* Place it in the root `app/error.js` as a global fallback.
* Layouts and templates don't catch errors from their children automatically – use a separate boundary.

A well‑designed app has multiple boundaries: the layout stays functional even if a specific panel crashes.

slides.title: Manual ErrorBoundary for Client Components (components/RiskyChart.js)
slides.content: Wrap a third‑party chart that might fail.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content: Combine `error.js` with `global-error.js` (for the root layout) to handle errors that crash the entire app, like those in the root layout itself.
